shape_free_floor_recomputation.verification_note: both released headline values (0.5286 on n=210, 0.2054 on n=1933) reproduce EXACTLY from the released features/seed. Confirmed, not corrected.

composition_exclusion_imbalance_test.class_balance_by_construction: the eval210 and train1610 splits are BOTH exactly uniform across the 7 crystal systems by stratified design (30/system and 230/system): split_meta.json per_system_train=230, per_system_eval=30 for all 7 systems. The composition-exclusion split does NOT induce crystal-system class imbalance -- the 32-point floor drop is not a class-imbalance artifact.

covariate_shift_found.space_group_granularity: eval210 has 44 distinct space groups across 210 structures (unique/n=0.210); train1610 has 128 distinct space groups across 1610 (unique/n=0.080) -- the eval draw is MORE space-group-diverse per structure, consistent with composition-exclusion selecting rarer, less-common compositions
covariate_shift_found.low_density_orthorhombic_outliers: 17/30 orthorhombic eval structures have density<2 g/cm^3 (median 0.56-1.10 g/cm^3), driven by large-cell dilute Tc/Os/Ir/Re-bearing intermetallics (e.g. [Al,Co,Tc], [Al,Fe,Tc]) that are reserved-element artifacts of MP's sparse coverage of these elements at low n_sites; train1610 has the equivalent share (37/230=16%) but at higher median density, so this is a magnitude shift within-class rather than a between-class imbalance

composition_exclusion_imbalance_test.conclusion: The composition-exclusion split preserves exact 7-way class balance (verified from split_meta.json and directly from eval.jsonl/train.jsonl). It does NOT explain the floor's 0.5286->~0.21 drop by class-imbalance. What it does induce is a COVARIATE shift in density and volume (both p<0.01) within each class -- reserved elements (Cd,Ce,Hg,In,Ir,La,Mn,Os,Re,Ru,Tc,Ti,Tl) are disproportionately heavy/dilute or rare-composition MP entries, and the eval210 draw of 210 out of the resulting ~350-450 eligible structures per system landed, by chance of the specific seed=23 draw, on a set where (n_sites,density,volume) happen to separate the 7 systems unusually well.

drop_mechanism_established_by_prior_reco.source: results/eval_scaleup/ (already computed; recomputed and confirmed here, not re-derived independently)
drop_mechanism_established_by_prior_reco.finding: the floor's drop from 0.5286 to ~0.21 is NOT a cell-size effect (unlike the oracle's drop, which reverses to 0.9459 under a size-matched control) and IS a property of the specific original n=210 draw: an independently drawn, identically stratified, composition-excluded n=1995 sample gives 0.2090 (0.2054 after quarantine), and a cell-size-matched n=721 subset of that draw still gives 0.2205 -- both far below 0.5286 and stable to cell size.
drop_mechanism_established_by_prior_reco.this_record_adds: a bootstrap resampling test on the n=1933 pool: 200 stratified 210-structure resamples (30/system) drawn from the SAME quarantine-clean population give a floor score of 0.2055 +/- 0.0222 (range 0.143-0.271), and ZERO of 200 draws reach 0.5286. A parallel test resampling composition-exclusion splits with 150 different random 13-element reservation sets from the original 1820-structure pool gives floor scores of 0.3196 +/- 0.0654 (max 0.4905), also never reaching 0.5286. A third test of 100 purely-random (non-composition-excluded) stratified n=210 draws from the same pool gives 0.4517 +/- 0.0314 (max 0.5190), still below 0.5286. The released 0.5286 sits above the maximum of all three resampling distributions: z=2.4 above regime C's mean, z=3.2 above regime B's mean, and z=14.6 above regime A's mean (regime A has the tightest spread, sd=0.0222, so the same absolute gap of 0.323 registers as a much larger z there). It is an upper-tail outcome of the specific seed=23 draw under every regime tested, most extremely relative to same-pool stratified resampling.
drop_mechanism_established_by_prior_reco.verdict: the 32-point drop is real and reproduces exactly, but its DIRECTION is not that composition-exclusion depresses the floor from a normal ~0.53 task-level value to ~0.21 -- it is that the released n=210 draw is an atypically high outlier for this 3-feature floor, and ~0.21-0.32 is closer to what the floor scores on typical draws of this size and design. This is stated as a property of the ORIGINAL 210 DRAW (design + sampling luck), not attributable to composition-exclusion as a mechanism, and not attributable to a flaw in the floor classifier itself (its exact reproduction from released features/seed rules out an implementation bug).

majority_class_vs_leaderboard.statement: the best zero-shot model (llama-4-maverick / glm-4.6v tied, 0.4429) beats the seven-way majority-class rate (0.1429 on the stratified n=210 sample) by 0.30 absolute -- it clears the weakest possible baseline decisively. It falls below the original 210-sample 3-feature shape-free floor (0.5286) but above that same floor's value on the full-scale, independently drawn, quarantine-clean sample (0.2054). The manuscript's below-floor claim is therefore sample-scoped, not a task property, but the model beating majority-class prediction is unambiguous and currently absent from the manuscript.
